messages.author: 4da793840121242b
messages.subject: Re: constraining factors
parts:
yes, below is my model specification. 'f2' is a factor and 'y2' is a 0/1 variable. What I would like to do is to set f2 positive when y2=1 and f2 negative when y2=0. Any suggestions?

model1 <- '#
y1 ~  NA*x
y2 ~ NA*f2
f2 =~ NA*x
#variances and covariances
y1~~f2
y1~~y1
y2~~y2
f2~~1*f2
# intercept
y1 ~ 1
f2 ~ 1
# constrains
y2==1*(f2>0)
'

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: constraining factors
parts:
On 06/13/2013 09:25 PM, Susana Eyheramendy wrote:
>
> yes, below is my model specification. 'f2' is a factor and 'y2' is a 0/1
> variable. What I would like to do is to set f2 positive when y2=1 and f2
> negative when y2=0. Any suggestions?

I have no idea what you are looking for. Factors (like f2) are latent
variables. We assume they are normally distributed, and all we can
'constrain' are the mean and variance of the factor.

Perhaps you could explain what 'f2',y2,x,... stand for, and why you wish
to constrain the factor f2?

Yves.

messages.author: 4da793840121242b
messages.subject: Re: constraining factors
parts:
y2 is 0/1 variable that I assume distributes as probit, that is why the latent  f2 appears which has a truncated normal distribution that I assume is correlated with y1 which is normally distributed. Does this make sense to you? Do you think it is possible to fit such a model with lavaan?

Many thanks,
Susana

good starting point.
